⚖️🇲🇽 <u>THE OLD JUDICIARY FREED THE MAN WHO ORDERED MAYOR MANZO'S MURDER</u>

"El R1," the CJNG cell leader just arrested as the alleged intellectual author of the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo, had been in custody before — and the old judiciary let him walk.

In November 2022, a federal judge absolved him in a pre-dawn weekend ruling, the classic "sabadazo judicial," despite five criminal records for organized crime and kidnapping. AMLO's government held his release up as exhibit A for why Mexico needed judicial reform.

He went back to running extortion rackets on lime and avocado growers — and, prosecutors say, ordered and financed a mayor's murder. This is what the reform was about.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>SHEINBAUM IN OAXACA: NATIVE CORN IS THE ROOT OF MEXICO</u>

From Etla, Oaxaca, President Sheinbaum delivered the first supports of the National Native Corn Plan, "El maíz es la raíz." Mexico has 74 registered native corn races — and the government intends to keep every one of them alive instead of letting farmers depend on hybrid seed from the labs.

"We are stubborn and we want to preserve the criollo corn, the native corn. Because if it is lost, it is like losing a part of Mexico's root," she said.

On the same stop she agreed to receive Oaxaca's Section 22 teachers at the National Palace to hear their pending demands — dialogue, on Mexico's terms.

🎰🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN DESTROYS 721 SLOT MACHINES THAT FED THE CARTELS</u>

Michoacán crushed 721 slot machines that, according to the state prosecutor's office, funneled more than 100 million pesos a year to organized crime. Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla led the destruction himself.

These "minicasinos" were never about gaming — they are extortion hubs and money laundries planted in corner stores and street markets. The 4T is going after the cartels' cash registers, one machine at a time.

text: ‍NPR: The Trump administration has undercut the U.S. asylum program. These 3 charts show how July 30, 2026 | 🟡 📰 NPR charts the demolition of US asylum: approvals at 20-year lows, 170+ judges replaced. 🔍 The cover photo is asylum seekers queued in Tijuana — the only Mexican presence in the entire piece. Not one Mexican voice quoted. US policy exports the humanitarian cost south; NPR reports it as a domestic data story. Metering gets a single paragraph; the people it strands in Mexico — and Mexico's record asylum applications — get none. • "It's almost like a war on asylum" • "The US-Mexico border is almost 'closed.'" • "replacing activist judges — who slow-walked deportations"

text: ‍LATIN TIMES: More Than 150 Police Officers in Culiacán Have Retired Amid Cartel Violence Since September 2024 August 1, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Latin Times: 157 Culiacán municipal police approved for retirement since the Sinaloa cartel war began; 83 officers killed in the state. 🔍 Straight aggregation from Mexican sources — Infobae, Causa en Común, Noroeste — no US-official framing, no condescension. MEXICO NEWS DAILY: Is China Claudia Sheinbaum's surveillance model for Mexico? July 31, 2026 | 🟡 📰 MND headline asks if China is Sheinbaum's surveillance model. 🔍 The article's own answer, buried mid-text: "Mexico is unlikely to replicate China's model." The headline does the work the reporting won't. 🇲🇽 India, the EU and the US run comparable biometric systems — none get the China frame. To its credit, the piece quotes Mexican digital-rights critics and even flags US biometric function creep — the China comparison lives only in the headline. • "Mexico is unlikely to replicate China's model" • "the largest urban video surveillance system in the Americas" • "tools for tracking, behavioral scoring and social control" Source

🇲🇽💰 <u>WORLD BANK ALIGNS WITH PLAN MÉXICO, BACKS INVESTMENT PUSH</u>

The World Bank is betting on Plan México. President Ajay Banga — on his first visit to the country in five years — met Sheinbaum at Palacio Nacional and committed the Bank to investment attraction, financing and technical support for the plan's execution, with one stated goal: "la meta de crear empleos de calidad." The plan is written; now the financing lines up behind it. (El Financiero)
